description:
PROBLEM: tests/unit/scripts/publication/test_check_explorer_compat.py::test_script_help_examples_name_the_current_version_and_all_run (22.7 s CI) starts 9 Python processes, each paying ~4 s of imports; tests/unit/scripts/test_corpus_privacy_invariant.py::test_anonymizing_the_corpus_twice_matches_anonymizing_it_once (16.8 s) and ::test_rederived_corpus_publishes_byte_identically_to_what_is_stored (8.9 s) both run the same first anonymization pass over the 419 primary bundles.

CHANGES:
1. Explorer: run each help example in-process via the checker's main(argv) after monkeypatch.chdir; read the help text via pytest.raises(SystemExit) plus capsys. Keep test_script_runs_as_the_deploy_workflow_invokes_it as the fresh-process check.
2. Corpus: merge the two tests into one pass per file: primary bundles compare canonical bytes with what is stored; files the pass changed are re-anonymized once and must not change; files the first pass left unchanged are already fixed points (anonymization is a pure function of value and salt) and are not re-run. Assertion messages must name the failing file and which property failed.
3. Update the two references to the merged byte-identity test id: .github/workflows/sync-results-data-to-published.yml (its error message) and docs/internal/results-phase-2-runbook.md; both files are in scope for C4.

EXCLUDED: a substring prefilter for the Windows antipattern scanner (lint-step speed, not a medium test; after longtest-01 D5 the lint job is its only consumer).

DECISION GATES:
G1 Explorer: show the deploy-workflow test still runs at least one example as a subprocess (fresh-process bootstrap coverage).
G2 Corpus: C2 mutations: (a) make anonymization non-idempotent for one key path and show the merged test fails on idempotence; (b) change one stored byte in a temp copy of a primary bundle and show it fails on byte identity. Purity: show anonymize_result_payload depends only on value and salt (file:line); if it reads any other state, keep the second pass for all files.
G3 C8: the explorer test moves from subprocess to in-process, so its script lines enter the coverage map; state this.
